comments.body:
Correction this is a problem with the HTML UI, which sticks the /fcr:metadata on the end.

i.e.

Create a binary, edit it’s metadata, delete it (preferably taking a second or more for each action to get 3 mementos).

eg. http://localhost:8080/rest/some-binary

Access the first or second memento with HTML UI

eg. http://localhost:8080/rest/some-binary/fcr:metadata/fcr:versions/20240228211850

Then choose the last memento, and end up at

http://localhost:8080/rest/some-binary/fcr:versions/20240228211935/fcr:metadata

fcr:metadata is in the wrong location and this causes the stacktrace.

This should probably not throw a Stack trace and could be caught and dealt with in FedoraId.

https://github.com/fcrepo/fcrepo/blob/main/fcrepo-kernel-api/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/kernel/api/identifiers/FedoraId.java#L485

Jared Whiklo something strange I’m seeing - it seems like the only time the 500 is produced is when using jetty:run. When running in tomcat or with the one-click I get a 400 response {{Invalid request for memento at $

{memento}

}} and a constrainedBy link header. I’m wondering if the jetty config is causing the exception mapper to not register correctly. Going to dig a bit more to see if there’s anything obvious missing.
Oh, the 500 is because the exception is being thrown from the WebACFilter so the exception ends up being handled by shiro instead of the exception mapper.

Ahhh okay that makes sense. So this is why I was thinking of the FedoraId, because we generate it here (https://github.com/fcrepo/fcrepo/blob/main/fcrepo-auth-webac/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/auth/webac/WebACFilter.java#L214 ) and then catch any errors to return a better error message here (https://github.com/fcrepo/fcrepo/blob/main/fcrepo-auth-webac/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/auth/webac/WebACFilter.java#L246-L248 ).

renderedFields.description:
Due to the changes in https://fedora-repository.atlassian.net/browse/FCREPO-3882 when you try to access the final version of a binary using the HTML UI it throws a 500 Server Error.

This is because while the http://localhost:8080/rest/some-binary will return the 410 Gone, the HTML UI automatically tries to go to http://localhost:8080/rest/some-binary/fcr:metadata and that throws the stack trace.
